verses.1: For the director. Do not destroy. A miktam of David, when he fled from Saul into a cave.
verses.2: Have mercy on me, God, have mercy on me. In you I seek shelter. In the shadow of your wings I seek shelter till harm pass by.
verses.3: I call to God Most High, to God who provides for me.
verses.4: May God send help from heaven to save me, shame those who trample upon me. May God send fidelity and love. Selah
verses.5: I must lie down in the midst of lions hungry for human prey. Their teeth are spears and arrows; their tongue, a sharpened sword.
verses.6: Show yourself over the heavens, God; may your glory appear above all the earth.
verses.7: They have set a trap for my feet; my soul is bowed down; They have dug a pit before me. May they fall into it themselves! Selah
verses.8: My heart is steadfast, God, my heart is steadfast. I will sing and chant praise.
verses.9: Awake, my soul; awake, lyre and harp! I will wake the dawn.
verses.10: I will praise you among the peoples, Lord; I will chant your praise among the nations.
verses.11: For your love towers to the heavens; your faithfulness, to the skies.
verses.12: Show yourself over the heavens, God; may your glory appear above all the earth.

notes.text: Do not destroy: probably the title of the melody to which the psalm was to be sung.
The shadow of your wings: probably refers to the wings of the cherubim (powerful winged animals) whose wings spread over the ark in the inner chamber of the temple (
I will wake the dawn: by a bold figure the psalmist imagines the sound of music and singing will waken a new day.
